previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A man with a history of systolic heart failure, COPD, and homelessness was admitted for acute shortness of breath and volume overload after his medications were stolen, leading to six days without diuretics. He presented with orthopnea, leg and abdominal swelling, and a productive cough. Elevated BNP and chest imaging confirmed heart failure exacerbation with mild pulmonary edema, and he was treated with IV furosemide followed by transition to oral torsemide 60 mg. A concurrent COPD exacerbation was managed with prednisone and doxycycline. His symptoms improved, weight decreased to near dry weight, and electrolytes remained stable. The PACT team assisted with medication security planning due to housing instability. He was discharged home with instructions to continue antibiotics and steroids, monitor daily weights, and follow up as scheduled.

Discharge Instructions:
Dear Mr. ___,

You were admitted to the hospital because you had some shortness 
of breath from your heart failure.  You received IV medicines to 
get the water out of your lungs.  You must take your medicine 
everyday. Weigh yourself every morning, call doctor if weight 
goes up more than 3 lbs.

You also had signs of withdrawing from alcohol.  We had hoped 
you would stay another day to make sure you did not have any 
issues with stopping alcohol, but you wanted to go home.  Please 
talk to your doctor about alcohol detoxification programs.  

Please continue to take all of your medications. At the least 
you MUST take your TORSEMIDE, METOPROLOL, SPIRONOLACTONE, and 
LISINOPRIL. Failure to take these medications will result in 
worsening of your heart failure.

Also, please refrain from alcohol. Heavy alcohol use will also 
worsen your heart failure and can cause liver disease.

It was a pleasure taking care of you,
Sincerely,

- Your ___ Team
